# Memory and memory import (area `memory`)

What FERB remembers about the owner, how it is recalled within limits, and importing memory from other assistants.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **MEM-1** (owner): FERB keeps the owner fact store. Procedure learning is replaced by a short "how I did it" note on each verified episode, retrieved by search for similar requests.
- **MEM-2** (owner): Forgetting a fact deletes the fact, its versions and its watcher-captured sources (trail rows), and blocks it from being re-learned. The owner's chat message that stated it stays: chat history is the owner's own record. FERB's past answers and traces are not scrubbed.
- **MEM-3** (owner): For memory, the owner's pass verdict counts as verified, as the checker's pass does; the owner's fail overrides the checker. The owner's latest verdict decides.
- **MEM-5** (owner): Memory has three tiers. Tier 1, the core profile, is always on in every role's prompt within a hard budget (about 2-3k tokens). Tier 2, the versioned fact store, holds everything. Tier 3 holds verified episodes with their how-notes, and playbooks. Everything outside Tier 1 is retrieved within limits, so prompts don't grow with memory.
- **MEM-6** (owner): Memory retrieval fuses a local embedding model running on the Mac with keyword search (bm25); the same search serves facts, episodes and old chat.
- **MEM-7** (owner): A change to a fact in the profile updates the profile at once, by code, with no model. A weekly model pass (sooner when over budget) compacts it: the model chooses and groups entries, code renders them from the facts, so the owner's words are never paraphrased.
- **MEM-8** (owner): The planner's remember rule and the daily distill's chat pass capture durable facts about the owner said in passing, not only after "remember ...". A fact FERB paraphrases is saved as FERB's understanding (MEM-12).
- **MEM-9** (owner): No special exclusion of health or finance facts in the planner or the distill. Secrets are masked by redaction as always.
- **MEM-10** (owner): Code stores what a remembered quote is about (from the task) next to the owner's exact words, so a line like "ok. score this 1 star - not ordering this again" still makes sense later. The words themselves are never reworded.
- **MEM-11** (owner): Forgetting a person or site also removes it from the known destinations, so a send to it asks again.
- **MEM-12** (owner): FERB saves facts itself, what the owner states and what it works out, each labelled by origin (the owner's words / FERB's understanding / observed). No Keep/Edit/Drop questions: a quiet "Memory: noted ..." line the owner can ignore or correct by talking. Memory never authorizes an action. A memory page in the app shows and edits everything.
- **MEM-13** (owner): From installed apps and their usage FERB works out what the owner mostly does, their most-used apps, main browser and main profile/account in it; it shows that once as "here's what I saw: ..." (no yes/no loop), stores it as observed facts, and refreshes it as usage changes. What holds up is promoted into Tier 1.
- **MEM-14** (owner): FERB's own understanding and observed facts that look over are retired automatically and the owner is told once. The owner's own words are retired automatically only when their recorded end date passes; otherwise FERB tells the owner once "this looks over, I'll stop using it", stops using it, keeps it as history, and restores it when the owner says it still holds.
- **MEM-17** (agent): PROFILE_TOKENS = 2,500 (within MEM-5's about 2-3k), counted as FERB's context counts (4 characters a token). Every render stops at the budget; what is left out is counted in one line and makes the profile pass due.
- **MEM-20** (agent): The pass runs weekly, or sooner when over budget, at most one try an hour; an owner fact that doesn't fit makes it due early, at most once in 24 h (EARLY_PASS_HOURS). The model returns sections of ids and `ended`; code refuses ids that don't hold up, renders every entry word for word, retires the ended ones ("FERB's weekly check") and tells the owner once in chat.
- **MEM-21** (agent): The planner looks up similar existing facts when a new one may replace one (memory.read, ORCH-515; Tier 1's facts are in its prompt) and names any a new fact replaces (`replaces`, ids checked by code); the "Memory: noted" line names what was replaced. A version resting on the owner's words now ends every current version of its fact and the named ids that hold; any other version never ends one the owner stated. Identical words are credited to the existing item (the owner's first), never a twin.
- **MEM-23** (agent): A known destination goes when its stored value is whole words of the forgotten item's content, label or subject name; a host also by its bare host or its site label (4+ letters: "kaggle" for www.kaggle.com); a phone by its digits (6+). The "Forget for good?" list says which.
- **MEM-25** (agent): The embedding model is minishlab/potion-base-8M (MIT, pinned revision and SHA-256s), a static table (29,528 WordPiece tokens x 256 float32; a text = the normalized mean of its tokens' rows), read by FERB's own tokenizer and memory-mapped safetensors: no numpy, torch, MLX or onnxruntime. Its vocabulary is English-only; other languages and coined words fall back to keywords.
- **MEM-26** (agent): The model files ship in FERB.app (Contents/Resources/models/embeddings/<name>@<rev12>) and are read there, never fetched by the app; a checkout's setup fetches them at install into ~/.ferb/models/embeddings (temporary folder, hashes checked, then renamed); `[memory] embedding_model` can name a folder. Until the model is there, search runs on keywords and recency. Tests never download.
- **MEM-27** (agent): Worker and plan step: facts + learned items <= 2,000 tokens and <= 10 items, no pushed chat, today's activity <= 2,000 tokens. The background attention check (tool-less): facts + learned items <= 4,000 tokens and <= 20 items (search.ATTENTION). The planner is pushed no memory, chat or activity (2026-11-03, ORCH-515): it looks them up. What doesn't fit is one counted line naming memory.read / memory.learned / trail.query. Lookup tools rank at most 100.
- **MEM-29** (agent): Code groups verified cards by goal similarity (PLAYBOOK_SIMILARITY 0.5); one model call says same kind or not and writes the steps; code checks the ids. At most 3 merges an hourly pass, only while no task runs, at most the 6 newest runs per call. A playbook is rewritten as new runs join; the owner's edit is never replaced; a declined group is not asked again.
- **MEM-30** (agent): A card keeps every episode, journal and memory ref, and one ref per distinct origin set of the others; its origin labels are computed from all refs.
- **MEM-31** (agent): A how-note is built from the worker's `how`, the owner's hints to the running task (quoted with their origin, 300 characters each) and the steps the card's recorded tool calls show (at most 12 steps, 600 characters). It is shown for verified runs only.
- **MEM-32** (agent): An owner fact that looks over (MEM-14) is set aside in `memory_set_aside`, beside memory_items: out of prompts, search and the profile at once, kept as history, restored when the owner says the same words again or by memory.restore. The login username it gave stays (it is still theirs and current).
- **MEM-33** (agent): Every turn records the memories it was given (`context.exposure`), so a repeated owner correction ("I told you before") traces to a memory miss and repeat runs show whether a how-note or playbook was used.
- **MEM-34** (agent): memory_items is the source of truth for facts, versioned, with source and validity window. No fact or identity copies live in learning_nodes. Facts tied to a period carry an end date (`until`) or a review date (`review_in_days`).
- **MEM-35** (owner): The owner's own words join Tier 1 at once only when they are about the owner. What the owner says about other things is placed by the weekly profile pass like any other fact.
- **MEM-400** (owner): FERB imports what matters about the owner from the major AI assistants they use (web, CLI and Mac apps), with schema-based extraction per assistant. Accuracy and recall are what count, and many model calls are acceptable; the result must make sense in FERB's memory and actually help it.
- **MEM-402** (owner): Every imported fact is saved as FERB's understanding (`inferred`), never as the owner's own words, and an import never adds known destinations.
- **MEM-404** (owner): The import extracts facts, preferences, projects, people and recurring tasks (as FERB's understanding); the raw imported chats are held in memory only while read, never stored or made searchable.
- **MEM-405** (owner): Extraction runs on the configured AI service; texts are redacted before they leave the reader module, and storage stays on the Mac.
- **MEM-407** (agent): Owner lines are: ChatGPT `user`, claude.ai `human`, Gemini "Prompted" records, Claude Code typed turns (not meta, sidechain, tool result or compact summary; `turnOrigin` human where present; no SDK sessions or subagent files), Codex interactive sessions only (`source` cli/vscode). Custom instructions and claude.ai project instructions count; uploaded files, attachments and tool output are not read; injected tag blocks are dropped.
- **MEM-408** (agent): Recall candidates are kept only when they cite an owner message (or a saved-memory claim) with a quote that is whole words of it; a verifier's supported verdict is kept only when its quote is whole words of an owner message shown as evidence. Saved memories (ChatGPT, claude.ai, Claude Code) are claims: kept only when the verifier cites an owner message of that source. An undated claude.ai memory is dated as of the import, its owner words still within the window.
- **MEM-409** (agent): Facts merge by `same_as` or kind+subject+key, oldest first. Newer wins by when the owner said it (`memory_import_items.said_at`, else a held fact's save time): an older imported version is skipped, not inserted as history. A fact the owner stated in their own words is never replaced or duplicated by an import (counted `kept_owner`). `ended`/`until` set an expiry; `review_in_days` a review.
- **MEM-410** (agent): Each conversation part's hash is recorded when done (`memory_import_done`), in the same step its facts are saved, so re-importing the same export later reads only what is new and a restart resumes. A forgotten fact is never re-imported (its fingerprint).
- **MEM-411** (agent): Every import model call (recall and each verify) waits while a chat turn runs (`_wait_idle` inside `_call`); running tasks don't block it. Three failed chunks in a row stop the run ("failed", told once); a later start goes on.
- **MEM-412** (agent): Import calls use the worker runtime with no tools and typed output (as the distill and profile pass). Their spans are `model.learning` with roles `memory_import_recall`/`memory_import_verify` and the goal "import memory from <assistant>", never the input. The estimate says 2 × chunks model calls; the run's actual count is in `counts.model_calls`.
- **MEM-413** (agent): Texts are cut at a word boundary, the cut said in the text: an owner message at 6,000 chars, an assistant reply at 700 (it only corroborates), a saved memory at 6,000. A recall call reads chunks of about 24,000 chars; a verification call batches about 30,000.
- **MEM-414** (agent): Gemini Takeout records whose marker word isn't the English "Prompted" are not read; the JSON variant with `details` Request is. Gemini HTML times in a zone other than UTC/GMT are read in this Mac's zone.
- **MEM-415** (owner): Memory import covers ChatGPT, claude.ai, Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini; no other assistants are added for now.
- **MEM-416** (agent): A fact that only a running task's targets name (the permit task's username) is recalled into that task's worker and plan steps within their memory limits (2026-11-03: planner turns are pushed no memory and look it up, ORCH-515), with the parent task's goal shown above a step's own, even among many past tasks that share the goal's words.
- **MEM-417** (agent): The developer memory dashboard serves only requests that carry its token from its own origin and host; anything else is refused.
- **MEM-418** (agent): The episode card reader takes no arguments and opens only the database of the FERB home it finds itself; a request naming another home, or none, is refused.
- **MEM-419** (owner): What a memory capture saves as the owner's words is only the part of their message that states the fact, never the whole message: the planner's content and quote are those words (with any negation or condition that belongs to them), and code saves the owner's own spelling of that span.
- **MEM-420** (agent): items.owner_clauses saves, from the owner's words, the clause(s) that hold the planner's content as whole words: from the clause mark before it to the one after it (, ; : ! ? or a line break; never a period, so "prof." and "Dr." don't cut a clause). A negation or condition in the same clause stays; one a mark sets apart stays only when the content holds it, as the planner's prompt says. Replaces the re-review R5 rule that saved the whole line.
- **MEM-422** (agent): An episode card that can't be built is still tried once more on the next hourly pass and, failed twice on the same inputs, waits for them to change (unchanged). Each failure is journaled `memory.cards_failed` with the task id, the error and what follows (tried once more, or waits until its task changes). `Learning.stuck_cards` lists the parked ones; `doctor.check` returns them as `learning.stuck_cards` and `ferb doctor` shows each. The pointer to a nonexistent `ferb memory consolidate` (and its unused `force`) is gone.
- **MEM-423** (owner): The Mac profile scan's facts (MEM-13) join Tier 1 at once when saved, within its budget, labelled observed. For everything else MEM-15 stands unchanged: The owner's own words join Tier 1 at once (same turn). FERB's understanding and observed facts join once they hold up (seen on 2 separate days, or standing 7 days uncorrected), and their join adds one quiet "Now always on: ... (label)" note card with Correct / Forget, never a question. The profile stays within its budget; the weekly pass only chooses and groups. The profile text is identical between turns unless a profile entry changed.
- **MEM-424** (agent): The owner's words hold up at once; so do the Mac profile scan's facts (MEM-423): observed items resting on a `memory.mac_profile` journal row, which only `mac_profile.store` writes (`Memory.from_mac_scan`), setup's scan and each weekly re-interpretation alike. FERB's other understanding and observed facts hold up once their sources span two separate days, or once they have stood a full weekly pass (7 days) without being replaced, retired or forgotten. An item kept under an older build's Keep question holds up at once; the old setup dump never does.
- **MEM-425** (agent): Code joins at once, under "Recently said" while it fits, only facts whose `subject` is "owner": the owner's words (MEM-35; not a fact placed by search, memory.search_only), the Mac scan's facts (MEM-423), and FERB's other understanding or observations once a save shows them holding up (a second day). The owner's words about anything else wait for the weekly pass, which places them like any fact. A join that isn't the owner's words adds its "Now always on" card (the scan's joins: MEM-427). The pass is the only scheduled rewrite; the owner's pins survive it.
- **MEM-427** (agent): The scan's joins post no "Now always on" notice each. A scan the setup step or the chat's "here's what I saw" notice shows is their telling; Correct / Forget stay on the Memory page. A quiet weekly re-check (or a scan with nothing shown) whose facts join or take an entry's place in Tier 1 posts ONE notice carrying a note card per fact, after everything else (`PersonaReview._store`, `CoreProfile.holding_joins`). Scan facts an older build saved join at the next re-check or pass: no one-time upgrade step.
- **MEM-428** (owner): A fact that newly joins Tier 1 is added at the end of the prompt, after its cached part, instead of being inserted into the always-on profile in the instructions.
- **MEM-429** (agent): Every role's instructions carry Tier 1's settled block; entries joined since (code's join, the owner's pin) show at once in a "Newly always on" section right after the context's cached part (Supervisor._with_newly_always_on), labelled like Tier 1 entries, within the same budget. The block settles only when the prefix changes anyway: a daemon start, the weekly pass, an entry of the block removed or replaced, a chat's summary fold. A newly joined entry forgotten or corrected leaves at once without settling.
- **MEM-430** (agent): Supersedes ORCH-646 for every check that a quote is the owner's own words (ferb-memory terms::quoted, one implementation): plan parts, remembered items and their end dates, schedules and reminders, imported conversations. Each blank-line part passes by Python's character comparison or when its words (letters, numbers, marks), in order and unbroken, are words the owner typed, case aside. Only acceptance is loosened: owner_stated text is still their exact clause, and a forget's clause check stays Python's.
- **MEM-431** (agent): Refines MEM-420 (its "never a period" guarded "Dr." and "prof."): the clause holding the planner's content also ends at a period that ends a sentence: space or the text's end follows it and the word it closes is no abbreviation by shape (single letters joined by periods; one to four letters before a capital or number). A period inside a word (v2.1, kartikey.xyz) never ends one. No word list. Fixed against Python.
- **MEM-432** (owner): Supersedes MEM-403. The import reads ChatGPT and claude.ai from their data exports (web and Mac app, saved memories and projects where the export has them) and Gemini from Google Takeout. Claude Code and Codex CLI are read from what the owner typed into them on this Mac (~/.claude/history.jsonl and ~/.codex/history.jsonl), not from session transcripts; Claude Code's own saved-memory notes are still read, as claims the owner's own typed words must back. A transcripts folder the owner names is still read as transcripts.
- **MEM-433** (agent): For MEM-432. What was typed becomes one conversation per session per local day (id `<session>@<day>`, titled by its folder), so a session that grows only changes today's conversation and the import's progress by part hash (MEM-410) stays incremental with no new state. Lines that say nothing by their shape alone are dropped (empty once injected tags are dropped, a bare slash command, the tool's interrupted-turn marker), and so is an exact repeat of a line typed earlier in the window. No word list. Codex's folder is read from the first 64 KB of its session file's header, never the whole rollout.
- **MEM-434** (owner): An import adds as many facts as it finds; three chunks are read at once, each call still waiting for the owner's chat turn (MEM-411). The import runs on the model FERB's settings give and never picks, names or caps one; nothing beyond which browser or export to use is put in front of the owner.
- **MEM-435** (owner): The models real users have by default are the mid-tier ones; the import's yield and precision have to hold up on them, mostly irrespective of the model, and the import still never picks a model (MEM-434). The lab's recall and verify prompts, measured for this, wait for the owner's yes before FERB's are changed (T-1281).
- **MEM-436** (agent): Each checked fact is kept (memory_import_facts, migration 0067) with the conversation or session it came from and its place: a coding session's folder, or a chat's title; a saved memory has none. The place is the evidence scope reads (MEM-443) and is shown, never written into a line. Nothing of the chats is kept (MEM-404).
- **MEM-437** (agent): Fixed against Python (found in the lab on a real export). A claude.ai project marked is_starter_project was written by the site and is not read. A conversation with parent links is read along the branch the site shows: back from current_leaf_message_uuid, else the newest message; a prompt the owner edited away, or a retried answer, is left out. An export with no parent links is read as before.
- **MEM-438** (agent): Before FERB's reader: a missing path, an unfinished download, an empty file, a web page saved as .zip (an expired link) or a damaged zip says so plainly with where to get a new one; after it, an export with nothing recent says whether it is another site's. claude.ai's manifest (or its loose part zips) is read from exactly the conversations, memories and projects parts it names; a missing part is named with whether its 24-hour link expired, never the link. Each source's newest export is kept: an older one sends nothing and says so.
- **MEM-439** (owner): An import keeps its checked facts as evidence and saves only the profile's lines as memory items: each fact joins a line, changes it, becomes a new line, or is left out with a reason, which is kept and shown only when the owner asks.
- **MEM-440** (owner): FERB downloads only the parts it needs (conversations, memories, projects) into its own private folder, never the owner's Downloads, and never fetches the large artifacts part or the part holding login history and invoices. It deletes them as soon as the import has read every part (not earlier: an import can stop and resume). If the import fails or is cancelled it deletes them anyway after 24 hours and tells the owner. It never deletes an export file the owner gave it himself, and leaves the export mail in his inbox alone.
- **MEM-441** (owner): From what the owner typed into Claude Code and Codex FERB keeps a work log: one entry per session per day with the session's id, folder, day, prompt count and a short title, summary, topics and state, no prompt text. It is kept up to date as new sessions appear, kept until the owner deletes it, and searchable; a session is opened again only when asked. Entries are learned nodes of kind work_log found by memory.learned (with since/until on the session's day); reopening a session is typing into a terminal, which asks first (AGENTS.md rule 6).
- **MEM-442** (owner): The imported profile is kept as a memory from outside: FERB considers it, never takes it as certain or as the owner's instruction (MEM-402), and his corrections outrank every fact, at once and through every later import: his own words on a line are never replaced or repeated by an import; a line he removed is gone and the same thing said again is left out; a line he ended stays ended until he says it again after that; his scope is final.
- **MEM-443** (owner): A preference or setup rule the owner stated inside one project is not used as a general rule about him when its words tie it there. A line is general unless its own words tie it to a project or a tool, or he scopes it himself; where it was said is kept as evidence and shown, but ties nothing. A tied line is applied only there, and every role reads its scope on the entry (the memory item's about).
- **MEM-444** (owner): An offer whose newest evidence is up to 30 days old is offered; 30 to 60 days old, it is asked about once, in one short 'Are these still on?' of at most five, the newest first, inside the import's one notice; older than 60 days it is only listed. An offer is never asked about twice; with no answer it is not offered or acted on. His answer (done, not interested, or still open) is kept on the line.
- **MEM-446** (owner): What FERB could offer is shown after an import and kept as candidates for its suggestions, never done unasked (lab IMP-27, his 'yes to all others'); an offer is made only while its line is recent (30 days), not over, and nothing since shows it done. A line last said more than 30 days ago is kept, marked 'last said …' on its entry, and asked about once in the import's notice; nothing old is hidden or dropped. 7 days: an offer said that lately is never called past on its words alone.
- **MEM-448** (owner): After setup (once the coding assistants' question is settled) FERB asks once whether to bring in what ChatGPT and Claude know about him and which browser profile he is signed in on. On a profile FERB runs the process itself, one quiet watch per site: it requests the export there, checks his mail in that profile every 15 minutes, downloads only the parts it needs, imports them (MEM-439), deletes the file (MEM-440) and tells him once, warmly, what it learned. A site's confirmation is told to him and FERB waits. On No nothing changes and it isn't asked again.
- **MEM-450** (agent): For MEM-439, porting lab IMP-31, IMP-37, IMP-38, IMP-43, IMP-50. A line is a memory item's name fixed when made, with an id that never changes. Only facts no line holds go to import_place.md, each with the lines sharing its rarest words; a join credits the day, an update is a new version only when newer and different (old words kept); saves go through Memory::save. Corrections are read from the item (owner-stated, retracted or forgotten, retired). Scope is asked only when words or places change, shown in the item's about with 'last said' for old lines.
- **MEM-451** (agent): For MEM-448. A website's watch is an ordinary schedule (every 15 minutes, until met, the chosen profile in its scope, a `job` target naming it) the owner sees and can stop; unlike his schedules (ORCH-590) its runs are journaled and posted only when one fails or ends with gaps, once until a run goes well. The workers' memory.import (after browser.downloads, owner identity, never the checker's) takes only a path under FERB's downloads folder and starts the import, which deletes it when done.
- **MEM-452** (agent): For MEM-444. The import's one ask (offers 30 to 60 days old, then lines from a while ago, one numbered list) is FERB's own question (memory.offers), routed like a task's question: the owner's next message answers it. A model reads which numbers his words mean (import_answer.md); code applies it: an offer's answer is kept on its line, a line still on is current again, one he says is over is retired. The Memory page shows each imported line's scope and offer with buttons (memory.import.lines, .scope, .offer).
- **MEM-453** (agent): ask_owner refuses a kind ferb_orchestrator::steering::memory_questions doesn't take, whatever answers the seam, and a contract test reads every own-question call site in ferb-daemon and ferbd (literals, formats, constants) and checks each kind is in that table and in OWN_KINDS. A test stand-in skipping the table can't let a new kind through again.
- **MEM-454** (owner): For MEM-435. import_recall.md and import_verify.md are the lab's text: one recall for every source, five short tests with examples. Verify names one reading per candidate (`reading` replaces `supported` and `kind` in VERIFY_SCHEMA); code (import_extract::verdicts) turns it into kept or not and the kind; a project's key is "identity"; a person or project keeps that subject shape, else the owner's. Quote checks (MEM-408), redaction and facts only (MEM-404) are unchanged. The prompt leaves out the lab's cut-line note (T-1285).
- **MEM-455** (owner): While a memory import FERB tells the owner about goes on (his Yes to the coding assistants, a website's export, one he starts on the Memory page), FERB shows its progress in the chat on FERB.app and both phones, with the same look and words, and at the top of FERB.app's Memory page: the source, the stage, real progress, and what it has found so far; it ends as the import's one notice (MEM-445), never a second message.
- **MEM-456** (agent): For MEM-455. One fold, ferb-learning import_live::card, from code facts only: a told run's own progress events (parts read of parts planned, then batches placed; facts kept so far; parts left unread) and each website watch's records (a run under way; asked when its first good run ended; its last run's trouble; its next run). The daemon keeps it in memory, publishes it on memory.import.live, gives it as memory.import.status live and the phone's chat.status memory_import (held while locked). It ends when the run's notice is said or it is cancelled; quiet hourly updates never show it.
- **MEM-457** (owner): For MEM-455. While an import runs, the phones' Chat home page (PHN-626) shows the live card too, above the message box, identical on Android and iPhone; the card's 'N things found so far' wording stays.
- **MEM-458** (owner): Supersedes MEM-401. Every import (Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, claude.ai, Gemini) and the work log read only the last calendar month; anything older is not read. Every owner-facing line about the window says the last month.
- **MEM-459** (owner): Settings and the Memory page each have two switches. The coding assistants': off reads nothing, no updates, a run under way ends; on reads them now and keeps up. ChatGPT and Claude's: off requests and fetches nothing, cancels both watches and ends a run; on asks which browser profile, as at setup. What was learned stays. Only through memory.import.switch, sensitive on a phone.
- **MEM-460** (owner): Supersedes MEM-445. An import never adds anything to always on by itself, at once or by the weekly pass; its lines stay remembered and searchable, on the Memory page and in the import's one notice. What FERB thinks should be always on (a recent repeat, IMP-47) is listed in one easy-to-read list of plain sentences, grouped (how you like FERB to work, about you, your setup), each with Approve / Decline and Approve all / Decline all: Approve adds it as his pin, Decline keeps it remembered only. Answered items leave; it stays until done. One card in chat, on the Memory page and both phones.
- **MEM-461** (owner): For MEM-460. Imported lines an earlier build put in always on by itself are in the same review list, marked "Already always on"; they stay always on until he answers each (nothing changes behind his back). One he pinned himself on the Memory page counts as approved. Their "Now always on" notices in the chat are folded into the one list: marked (`folded`), never deleted, no client draws them again (as alerts are marked, APP-1106). Done at the start (once per line), with the review asked then.
- **MEM-462** (agent): For MEM-444, IMP-41, refining MEM-452. The review is one card of three parts, each its own question and buttons, never mixed: keep in mind all the time (MEM-460); "Are these still true?" for older lines (Yes / No, not any more / Not sure); "Still want help with these?" for offers 30 to 60 days old (Yes / Done already / No thanks). Item by item, all at once, or in his words (question memory_review). Older lines asked are only those steering FERB's work (preferences, setup, recurring things, projects), five at most, once; other facts stay, marked 'last said'.
- **MEM-463** (agent): Every "Now always on" notice goes through one path (`memory::tell_always_on`): joins within 1.5 s of each other (a learning pass, the weekly pass, the Mac scan's re-check) are one notice, "Now always on: N things (label)", with a note card per fact that FERB.app and the phones show as a list that opens ("Show all N" / "Show less"). One fact alone reads as before. A notice with more than one note card shows them that way.
- **MEM-464** (owner): For MEM-460 and MEM-461. The review is drawn as shown, the same on the Mac and both phones. An item already always on has Keep (it stays on, his pin) and Remove (it leaves always on and stays remembered); a group whose items are all already on has Keep all / Remove all; a part all already on has them in place of Approve all / Decline all. The words and buttons come from the engine; the apps only lay them out.
- **MEM-465** (agent): For MEM-460. `memory.review {}` answers the list as every client draws it (parts, groups, items, each item's and group's own buttons, all-at-once buttons, count); `memory.review.answer {part, item_ids, answer}` applies the owner's answer and answers the list as it stands; the question closes when nothing is left. From a phone both are private (the unlock window): an answer to FERB's own question, as chat.answer is, shown with his data. The Memory page's Always on / Not always on on an imported line is his answer to it as well (one path).
- **MEM-466** (owner): Supersedes MEM-447. FERB asks once after setup; on Yes it reads the coding assistants' last month once, places what it learns, writes the work log and tells him once. After that no model reads them unless he asks (in chat, or Bring in what's new on the Memory page), and then only what is new. Which sessions he has is kept by code alone (tool, folder, session, days, prompt counts), brought in step when something reads it. Settings turns it off; what was learned stays. On No nothing is read; offered again only if he asks.
- **MEM-467** (owner): Supersedes MEM-449. FERB requests each site's export itself (starting covers it; it may ask only which mailbox) and tells him when a site wants a confirmation, then waits. Waiting runs no model each time: the 15-minute ticks are code only; a model run checks the mail at most every 12 hours (FERB's proposal, his number to set) until a code check of the mailbox exists (T-1293). Past the provider's own stated time, FERB tells him so he can request it again or give the file.
- **MEM-468** (owner): Supersedes MEM-22 and MEM-421; refines MEM-8 (only the planner captures facts said in passing) and MEM-13 (the Mac scan isn't refreshed as usage changes). The hourly pass writes each past day's summary by code (`trail.day_summary`, which retention needs) and runs no model for it: no day narrative, no facts proposed or retired, no review dates checked. Stored narratives stay and are read as before. The weekly Mac re-check is off (MEM-469); the setup scan stays. Episodes, playbook merges and the weekly core-profile pass stay.
- **MEM-469** (agent): For MEM-468. Code gathers the 25 most-used apps (TOP_APPS), installed/used counts, browsers and Chromium profiles; one model call (mac_profile.md) writes the summary and facts, stored observed and active, in Tier 1 at once within its budget (MEM-423). Shown once. Gathered again only for the browser part a scan before Full Disk Access lacked (DMN-507), with no date gate; re-interpreted then only when facts_fingerprint changed (a new version takes its entry's place, a new key joins: MEM-7, MEM-427). No weekly re-check.
- **MEM-470** (agent): For MEM-468. A day whose summary fails is recorded `failed`, journaled `memory.distill_failed` with its tries, and tried again on the next hourly passes, at most 3 times in all (`distill::SUMMARY_TRIES`, FERB's proposal: T-1044 asks the owner). One day's failure never holds up the days after it; a day left unsummarized keeps its activity in the trail (retention purges only summarized days), and `ferb doctor` lists it.
- **MEM-471** (owner): Confirms, as his: the website watch's model check of the mail runs at most every 12 hours (`WATCH_MODEL_EVERY_HOURS`, MEM-467) until a code mailbox check exists (T-1293); `memory.review` and `memory.review.answer` are private from a phone, not sensitive (MEM-465); the review asks only about older lines that steer FERB's work, five at most, once, and keeps the others marked 'last said' (MEM-462).
